title: Echoes of Ten Thousand Years
next_chapter_hook: In the depths of that hazy memory, a sacrificed maiden slowly raised her head, her gaze startlingly similar to what Chen Ji saw in himself every night in the mirror.

text.content: That ancient voice rolled through his blood like thunder, and Chen Ji's Mental Sea trembled abruptly. The seal on the fifth page of the Tianji Record shattered on its own, golden runes surging through his meridians like fireflies, bringing searing pain and unprecedented fullness. He felt his consciousness being dragged by an irresistible force, down, down, falling into the endless abyss of darkness. The surrounding scenery dissolved in distortion—the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters, the flickering candlelight, Su Qingyao's worried gaze—all fading away.

Darkness was not emptiness. When his consciousness reached a certain critical point, specks of light began to appear before Chen Ji's eyes. They were stars—not stars in the night sky, but a vast chessboard composed of countless points of light. Each point of light was a life, and every thread of connection was a path of destiny. He had glimpsed Heavenly Secrets countless times, yet never had he witnessed such a magnificent sight. The Tianji Record Fragment's foresight was a stream, but what he now touched was an ocean.

"You've finally arrived." The ancient voice rang out again, no longer from the depths of his blood, but from all directions. Chen Ji猛然回头—he actually had the ability to turn around—and saw deep within the Void, a blurred figure standing with hands clasped behind its back. The figure was surrounded by a faint purple-gold radiance, its features hidden within the halo, impossible to discern. But that figure, that bearing—even blurred, it evoked an irresistible urge to prostrate in worship.

Chen Ji did not kneel. Gritting his teeth, he straightened his spine before this figure. The skin of a废物 servant could be worn, but the bones of a Chen family man could not bend. The figure seemed to emit a soft laugh: "Ten thousand years, and finally one with some spine." Before the words finished, the surrounding star chessboard suddenly expanded, ten thousand years of time flickering past Chen Ji's eyes like a carousel.

He saw—the world ten thousand years ago was far more splendid than now, Spiritual Energy so abundant it nearly condensed into substance. Countless sects dotted the heavens like stars, and the most dazzling was that palace floating above the Nine Heavens. Seven figures stood before the palace, each radiating an aura that made Chen Ji suffocate. They were the Chess Players of that era. And the one standing at the center—

Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. That seventh Chess Player's figure coincided perfectly with the figure from before. What shocked him more was that face—sword-like brows, star-bright eyes, deep-set features, and in those eyes, the same cold ruthlessness and calculation as Chen Ji. This was not similarity; this was bloodline continuation. The seventh Chess Player—that legendary ancient great one who had opposed the Heavenly Will single-handedly and ultimately perished—was directly connected to him by blood!

dialogue.content: Impossible... A figure from ten thousand years ago, how could he be my ancestor? The Chen family is just an insignificant, declining clan—what divine virtue do we possess...

text.content: "What divine virtue?" The ancient voice seemed to hear his thoughts, carrying a hint of mockery, "Do you think the Tianji Record can be wielded by just anyone? All Chess Players throughout history have come from the same source. Within the Chen bloodline flows the talent to peer into Heavenly Secrets. But this talent is too heaven-defying, so every generation of wielders cannot escape Heavenly Tribulation."

choice.prompt: Faced with the truth of ten thousand years ago, Chen Ji needed to make a choice: continue deeply exploring this bloodline memory, or stop while ahead and extract key information, or directly interrupt the deduction to preserve Heavenly Fate Value?

choices.description: Continue sinking into the memory, exploring more truth about the seventh Chess Player's confrontation with Heavenly Will. Extremely high risk, but may obtain key information.
choices.visible_reward: Unlock Hidden Chapters of Tianji Record
choices.risk_hint: Insufficient Heavenly Fate Value Will Trigger Fatal Backlash

text.content: Chen Ji did not hesitate. With a thought, his consciousness pierced into the depths of memory like a blade. The power of bloodline boiled within him, golden runes on the fifth page of the Tianji Record surged madly, dragging him toward an even more ancient era. "Courageous." The voice seemed to carry a hint of praise, "But do you know—the truth of that chess game ten thousand years ago is enough to drive any Chess Player insane?"

The scene suddenly sharpened—the seventh Chess Player stood before that Nine Heavens palace, behind him the bones of six companions. Before him was a massive eye that blotted out half the sky. The Eye of Heavenly Will. It was laughing, laughing so contemptuously. "You thought you could escape my chessboard?" The Eye of Heavenly Will's voice shook heaven and earth, "All Chess Players throughout history are my chess pieces. You are no exception."

dialogue.content: "Escape?" The seventh Chess Player let out a tragic laugh, the Tianji Record in his hand shattering with a thunderous roar, "I am not trying to escape. I am going to let you know—"

choices.description: Only extract the most critical information, do not explore deeply, to preserve strength for future challenges. Conservative but may miss opportunities.
choices.visible_reward: Confirm Bloodline Connection, Obtain Basic Inheritance

text.content: Chen Ji forced himself to冷静, quickly摄取 information at the edge of memory. The bloodline connection was confirmed—he was a direct descendant of the seventh Chess Player, and the Tianji Record choosing him was no accident. In that great war against Heavenly Will ten thousand years ago, the seventh Chess Player, at the cost of his fall, scattered the Tianji Record into several pieces across the mortal world, waiting for later worthy individuals to reassemble them.

"Enough." Chen Ji said in a low voice, his consciousness beginning to float upward. That aged voice rang out once more: "Steadiness, not greed—this is the secret to living long. But remember, the more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the fatal backlash of fate. Are you, truly, ready?"

dialogue.content: Chen Ji did not answer this question. Some answers are not spoken with the mouth.

choices.text: Interrupt deduction to preserve Heavenly Fate
choices.description: Immediately interrupt memory deduction, preserving precious Heavenly Fate for emergencies. Conservative but steady.
choices.risk_hint: May forever lose the chance to deeply understand the truth

text.content: Only thirty-seven points of Heavenly Fate remained. Every single point was life itself. Chen Ji had no hesitation, directly severing the connection with the bloodline memories. Consciousness was ejected from the darkness like a launch, and his vision spun wildly. When he opened his eyes again, he saw the familiar beams of the Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters, and Su Qingyao's face filled with worry.

"What just happened to you?" Su Qingyao's voice trembled slightly. "Your energy was in such terrible chaos, I almost thought..." She didn't finish, but the concern in her eyes was genuine. Chen Ji tugged at the corner of his mouth: "Just had a dream." He sat up, his mind racing—What did it mean that the Chess Player from ten thousand years ago had bloodline connections to him? Why did the Eye of Heavenly Dao treat the successive Chess Players as mere pieces? What role did Chen Nian play in all this?

dialogue.content: The enigmas multiplied, but at least one thing was certain—he was not fighting alone. The chess game that ancestor ten thousand years ago had laid out with his life, Chen Ji had accepted.

text.content: Regardless of how deep the exploration went, the memory images continued playing. The Seventh Chess Player's words enraged the Eye of Heavenly Dao, and that massive eye erupted with destructive light. However, at that moment, the Seventh Chess Player did something that shocked everyone—he divided his bloodline into several portions, sealing them within the fragments of the Tianji Record through secret methods, scattering them across the mortal realm. "Someday," his voice echoed through the shattered space-time, "my descendants will end you completely."

The scene shifted. After the Seventh Chess Player perished, the Eye of Heavenly Dao began purging all who knew the truth. The six Chess Players' companions, their sects, bloodlines, descendants—one and all, not a single survivor. Chen Ji saw countless people turn to ash amid wails, saw once-flourishing sects reduced to ruins overnight. And the fragments of the Tianji Record scattered everywhere, quietly waiting for the day they would be reclaimed.

text.content: Chen Ji condensed his consciousness into a single focal point, pursuing memory fragments about the Chen family from within his bloodline. He saw—ten thousand years ago, the Chen family had been the most loyal guardians of the Chess Players. When the Heavenly Dao's purge came, countless people betrayed and fled, only the Chen family held firm until the very last moment. Yet this also made them a primary target for the Eye of Heavenly Dao's eradication.

dialogue.content: So the Chen family did not decline because of weakness, but because—they were too powerful, too loyal, thus becoming marked by Heavenly Dao, weakened generation after generation.

choices.text: Examine the truth of the Tianji Record's seal
choices.description: Understand why the Tianji Record exists in fragment form, and the true reason behind the seal.
choices.visible_reward: Core secrets of the Tianji Record

text.content: The core area of the fifth page of the Tianji Record was shrouded in an eerie black mist. When Chen Ji's consciousness touched that layer of black mist, a bone-deep chill instantly devoured him. This was no ordinary cold—it was the freezing of fate. Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly rang out: "This layer, your current realm cannot yet touch. What is sealed there is one of the fragments of the Heavenly Eye."

Chen Ji's pupils constricted. The Heavenly Eye's fragment—sealed within the Tianji Record? What did this mean? Was the Tianji Record both a supreme treasure for divining heavenly secrets and a prison confining the Heavenly Eye's fragments? No wonder every generation of its keeper was purged by the Heavenly Dao, for what they held in their hands was not merely a tool, but a weapon.

dialogue.content: "Forefather, what kind of chess game are you playing?"

text.content: Just then, the memory's imagery suddenly began to distort. The seventh chess player's silhouette gradually faded, replaced by a blood-soaked altar. Around the altar stood numerous robed figures, their faces wearing fanatical expressions as they chanted ancient sacrificial incantations in unison. Chen Ji saw the stone pillar at the altar's center—and bound to it was a young girl, her body being stripped away inch by inch by an invisible force.

The girl's face was blurred beyond recognition, but her eyes—those eyes—Chen Ji's heart violently clenched. That gaze was identical to what he saw every night in the mirror. Cold, despairing, yet with an unyielding stubbornness. Her gaze seemed to pierce through time and space, staring directly at Chen Ji. Her lips quivered, silently uttering two words. Chen Ji understood those two words—"Save me."

Chen Ji's hand clenched abruptly, his knuckles whitening. Beneath the exterior of a废物杂役 disciple, that coldly calculating heart experienced its first violent tremor. Who was this girl? Why did she resemble Chen Nian so closely? Why was her gaze identical to his own? How did all of this connect to Chen Nian being taken by the Holy Sect? What kind of enormous chess game was the Heavenly Eye plotting?

Just as Chen Ji wished to see more clearly, that aged voice rang out once more: "Time is up. The Heavenly Fate Value is insufficient to sustain further divination. Moreover—" The voice paused, carrying a hint of gravity, "Her appearance signifies the Heavenly Eye has begun its net-drawing. If you do not wish to become a discarded piece, you must eliminate its chess pieces one by one before it makes its move."

Chen Ji offered no response, but his gaze had already given the answer. His ancestor from ten thousand years ago had used his life to lay out this chess game spanning millennia, waiting precisely for him—this successor. Since heavenly intent had made him a chess player, then Chen Ji—would engage in a game against this Heavenly Dao without hesitation. Consciousness began to float upward, and the memory's imagery receded like a tide. The girl's silhouette on the altar gradually blurred, yet her gaze was seared deeply into Chen Ji's heart.

When Chen Ji opened his eyes once more, most of the candles in the Servants' Quarters had already burned out. Su Qingyao still kept vigil by the bedside, faint dark circles beneath her eyes indicating a sleepless night. When she saw Chen Ji awaken, a flash of惊喜 crossed her eyes before she resumed that haughty demeanor: "Awake? Your spiritual energy fluctuated紊乱 for an entire night—what exactly happened?" Chen Ji sat up, feeling his Heavenly Fate Value completely emptied within his body, yet a faint smile curved his lips—that smile contained both the timidity of a废物杂役 and the sharpness of a chess player.

Su Qingyao frowned as she observed his changing expressions, a hint of探究 flickering in those sharp eyes. This servant disciple was becoming increasingly incomprehensible to her—his spiritual presence was pathetically weak, his realm laughably low, yet that occasional glint in his eyes made even her, an Inner Disciple Senior Fellow, feel a chill of dread. "Chen Ji," her voice lowered, "what exactly are you hiding?"

dialogue.content: "Hiding?" Chen Ji raised his head, a harmless smile appearing on that ordinary face, "Senior Sister Su worries too much. I'm merely a servant disciple—what could I possibly hide? I merely had a nightmare, in which I met my own ancestor." He stood up, stretching his stiff limbs, while his mind rapidly calculated. His Heavenly Fate Value had only thirty-two points remaining; he must find a恢复 method as soon as possible. And that sacrificed girl—no matter who she was, no matter what connection she had with Chen Nian, he would rescue her.

text.content: "Ancestor... is it?" Su Qingyao低声重复, a meaningful glint flashing across those eyes. She posed no further questions, simply turning to walk toward the door. At the threshold, her voice drifted back faintly: "The Tianqing Sect's triennial Inner Sect Assessment is next month. With your strength..." She paused, "Perhaps you could give it a try." With that, her figure vanished into the morning light, leaving Chen Ji alone standing in the Servants' Quarters, gazing at that departing silhouette.

Chen Ji knew Su Qingyao had begun her试探. But what of it? Since he had already chosen the path of a chess player, these sect disciples, elders, and even the sect master—were merely chess pieces on his board. He lifted his gaze toward the window, where the horizon had begun to glow pearl-white, a new day approaching. And deep within the fifth page of the Tianji Record, that aged voice seemed to sigh: "The chess game has begun—once a piece falls, there is no regret. Chen Ji—rather, I should call you, the Seventh Chess Player. Your road... is still long."
